Iran’s hard-line leaders huddled in Tehran and came up with a different plan, according to Iranian and Arab officials. In their view the pact was likely just an attempt by the U.S. and Israel to take pressure off the global economy and buy time for a bigger attack down the road. Instead of putting faith in talks, they took the past two months to prepare for a bigger fight. 

Their efforts include giving the powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps more control of the country’s regular army, appointing hardened veterans of the war with Iraq and past internal crackdowns to key posts, expanding domestic counterintelligence operations and ramping up production of missiles and drones. The leadership quickly seized the initiative, attacking ships to tighten Iran’s grip on Hormuz and expanding the battlefield to the Red Sea, which Saudi Arabia has used to get around Iran’s chokehold on the Persian Gulf.

#Bitcoin / bitcoin:native 

Think we see a bit more chop this month before one last leg down to the mid 40s to create the pico-bottom for the bear market.

September is typically a rough month for crypto and ~900 days post halving has marked the bottom the last several cycles.

Robinhood Chain eco is still my long hedge / e.g. think there's a high chance the momentum and growth we've seen carry into the ecosystem so far continues. It's where the "hot ball of money" is currently and where I expect it to continue to roll (e.g. similar to what HYPE did earlier this summer when the majority of the market bled).

One way or the other - market should be very close to a bottom from a time perspective.

End of 2026 into 2027 should be fun.

tweets.text: Pokemon card market still actively making ATHs, although the focus has branched out into the more obscure stuff which is a similar indicator to altseason in terms of where the cycle is imo. We have also seen a wave of fake goldstars on par with superfake watches, if you are not an expert you are not going to spot them. I am gradually selling into market strength. I think we have to reckon with a double-edged thesis here. Post-scarcity society means significantly greater capital for pastimes & attention share of brand names; Pokemon is the pinnacle of this. But with this comes bad actors empowered by AI and robotics; there is a realistic price cap on the card market where it becomes economically viable to run an industrial scale counterfeiting operation of flawless copies. This is a difficult to quantify tail risk, and I am not saying this is even realistic in the next few years, but I do wonder what the defensive options are here.
